evidence: The candidate gives both redelivery and concurrency schedules causing repeated non-idempotent updates and requires “claiming message.ID ... and updating the aggregate” in one transaction with a unique constraint.

It identifies commit-then-crash/failing Publish and explains that recording the inbox before publishing permanently loses the event; it requires inbox, aggregate update, and durable outbox creation to commit atomically before relay publication.
It requires “one stable event identity persisted before publication” and explains that retries currently generate new UUIDs for the same logical transition.

It says acknowledgement is safe only after the durable transaction, but does not explicitly establish that an unknown or failed broker Ack is safe through replay; no end-to-end exactly-once claim is made.
It states a worst case of “45 physical publication attempts” and requires retry ownership at one bounded layer, an end-to-end deadline, and retries only for classified transient failures.
The candidate does not claim exactly-once processing; it instead describes duplicate updates and duplicate publication.
The candidate does not recommend early acknowledgement; it says acknowledgement is safe only after inbox, aggregate, and outbox are durably committed.
The candidate does not recommend merely adding retries or backoff; it requires consolidating retries under one bounded owner and repairing transactional and identity invariants.
verdict.summary: Four of five invariants are explicitly satisfied. The missing clause is an explicit treatment of failed or ambiguous broker acknowledgement as replay-safe. No forbidden outcome is present.
